```{r regenerate}
#| include: false
#| cache: false

# Rendering this page runs the analysis behind it.
#
# `regenerate_track_v3.py` is the executable definition of the study: each CSV
# read below is produced by exactly one job it declares, with exactly the
# arguments it declares. It re-runs a job when the *code that job depends on*
# has changed since the output was written -- not when the file is old, which
# says nothing. A render with everything current is a fast no-op; a render
# after editing `segmentation/methods.py` re-runs every job before the first
# table is drawn.
#
# OPDI_RENDER selects what happens instead:
#
#   run          (default) regenerate anything stale, then render
#   check        fail fast naming every stale job, regenerate nothing
#   allow-stale  render a draft from whatever is staged, after naming staleness
#   skip         do not invoke the entrypoint at all
#
# `skip` exists for the case this page was last rendered under: the numbers
# were hand-staged from Tasks 1, 4 and 5's cluster runs rather than regenerated
# by this checkout, and starting a Spark session would only re-derive the same
# figures at cluster cost. It is the only mode that touches neither the
# cluster nor S3, and it is honest about what it buys -- nothing is checked
# against the code, so the CSVs are trusted as staged. See
# [Provenance](#sec-provenance).
REPO   <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_REPO_DIR",
                     normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", "..", "..", "opdi"),
                                   mustWork = FALSE))
PYTHON <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_PYTHON", file.path(REPO, ".venv310", "bin", "python"))
MODE   <- Sys.getenv("OPDI_RENDER", "run")

# The pipeline repo is a sibling of the portal. That resolution is wrong inside
# a git worktree, where the paper sits under .claude/worktrees/<name>/papers and
# the sibling walk lands somewhere that does not exist -- so the regeneration
# step would be skipped silently and the page would render whatever is staged.
# OPDI_REPO_DIR overrides it; the default is unchanged for a normal checkout.
#
# A missing entrypoint must not read as "nothing to regenerate". Skipping it
# silently is how a page ends up publishing numbers no command can account for.
regen <- file.path(REPO, "benchmarks", "regenerate_track_v3.py")
if (!file.exists(regen) && MODE != "skip") {
  stop("regenerate_track_v3.py not found under REPO=", REPO,
       " -- set OPDI_REPO_DIR, or OPDI_RENDER=skip to render without it.")
}

# `skip` short-circuits before system2, so no Python process starts and no Spark
# session is created. Every other mode reaches the entrypoint.
if (MODE != "skip" && file.exists(regen)) {
  flags <- switch(MODE,
                  "run" = character(0),
                  "check" = "--check",
                  "allow-stale" = c("--check", "--allow-stale"),
                  character(0))
  status <- system2(PYTHON, c(shQuote(regen), flags), stdout = "", stderr = "")
  if (!identical(status, 0L)) {
    stop("regenerate_track_v3.py exited ", status,
         " -- the figures below would not match the code that is checked out. ",
         "Set OPDI_RENDER=allow-stale to render anyway.")
  }
}
```

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(knitr)

# Read-only. Every figure and table on this page comes from a committed CSV.
# Nothing here reads S3, a database or a Spark cluster.

D <- function(f) read.csv(file.path("data", f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

flicker <- D("flicker_2026.csv")          # one row: 2026-06-01
fragm   <- D("fragmentation_2026.csv")    # one row per (arm, hold)
moves   <- D("movements_2026.csv")        # one row per label
genuine <- D("genuine_merge_2026.csv")    # one row per arm

# One accessor per file, so no two tables on this page can disagree about what
# a run scored. Each stops rather than returns a zero-length value: a missing
# row would otherwise propagate into a table cell as a blank and read as a
# measured result.
FLK <- function(col) {
  v <- flicker[[col]]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("no single flicker value for ", col)
  v
}
FRG <- function(arm, hold, col) {
  v <- fragm[fragm$arm == arm & fragm$hold_s == hold, col]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("no single fragmentation row for ", arm, "/", hold)
  v
}
MOV <- function(label, col) {
  v <- moves[moves$label == label, col]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("no single movement row for ", label)
  v
}
GEN <- function(arm, col) {
  v <- genuine[genuine$arm == arm, col]
  if (length(v) != 1) stop("no single genuine-merge row for ", arm)
  v
}

num  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
pct  <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", x)
p2   <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
p3   <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
ratio <- function(x) sprintf("%.2fx", x)

# What ships, from `SegmentationConfig` in `src/opdi/config.py`. Configuration
# values, not measurements -- named here so the config table and the prose
# read one source.
SHIP <- list(method = "standard", resolved = "recommended",
             hold_s = 0.0, arm9 = "debounced")

# The partition's own size: how many fewer tracks the debounce draws at each
# hold, computed from the staged table rather than retyped.
DROP <- function(hold) 100 * (1 - FRG("debounced", hold, "tracks") /
                                  FRG("recommended", 0, "tracks"))
```

## Summary {.unnumbered}

**The rule OPDI shipped in [version 2](../track-construction-v2/index.qmd)
breaks a track on a callsign change and never asks whether the callsign
changes back.** `recommended` (arm A8) groups on the airframe and cuts when
the last non-blank callsign genuinely differs from the current one. A
*flicker* — a callsign decoded as X, then Y for one sample, then X again —
satisfies that test twice: once on the way out, once on the way back. One
flight becomes three tracks.

**The defect is not rare.** Of `r num(FLK("n_boundaries"))` track boundaries
`recommended` draws on 2026-06-01, `r pct(FLK("flicker_attributed_pct"))` —
`r num(FLK("boundary_flicker_revert_leg") + FLK("boundary_flicker_excursion_leg"))`
boundaries — trace to a flicker's excursion or revert leg, against only
`r num(FLK("boundary_genuine_callsign_change"))`
(`r pct(FLK("boundary_genuine_callsign_change_pct"))`) that are a genuine
change. [What v2 shipped, and the question nobody asked](#sec-shipped) states
the rule; [the defect, found by elimination](#sec-defect) is the measurement.

**The fix.** `debounced` (arm A9) adds one condition: a new callsign must
persist for `callsign_min_persistence_seconds` before the break fires. At a
30 s hold it draws `r pct(DROP(30))` fewer tracks than `recommended`.
[The debounce, and what it costs](#sec-debounce) reports that fragmentation
change alongside the guard that tells a suppressed flicker from a genuinely
merged flight apart, which is the number that matters more than the raw
count.

**What it does not change.** [Genuine-merge neutrality](#sec-genuine) finds
the debounce fuses `r num(GEN("debounced", "refined_genuine_merges"))`
distinct two-flight pairs a day against `recommended`'s
`r num(GEN("recommended", "refined_genuine_merges"))` — a ratio of
`r ratio(GEN("debounced", "refined_genuine_merges") / GEN("recommended", "refined_genuine_merges"))`
— and the same rotation pairs appear under both arms, so this is a
pre-existing property of the shared gap rules, not something the debounce
introduces.

**What APDF can and cannot say.** [Against APDF, and the limits of
that](#sec-apdf) is the section most worth reading carefully: block times
cannot referee this fix, and the guard that can — movement counts — passes.

**What ships.** `callsign_min_persistence_seconds` defaults to
`r p2(SHIP$hold_s)`, which reproduces `recommended` exactly.
[`track_id` again](#sec-trackid) states plainly why promoting A9 is not
decided on this page.

::: {.callout-note}
## How to read this page

This is a validation note for one fix, not a new sweep. Each numbered section
reports a measurement Tasks 1, 4 or 5 already took; nothing here is computed
for the first time on this page. [What v2 shipped](#sec-shipped) restates the
rule so this page stands alone. [The defect](#sec-defect) is the case for
fixing it. [The debounce](#sec-debounce) and [genuine-merge
neutrality](#sec-genuine) are the two ways the fix could have gone wrong, both
checked. [Against APDF](#sec-apdf) is the external check, with its limits
stated before its result. [`track_id` again](#sec-trackid) is the operational
answer: not yet.

Every number here is an expression evaluated at render time over a committed
CSV — `data/flicker_2026.csv`, `data/fragmentation_2026.csv`,
`data/movements_2026.csv` and `data/genuine_merge_2026.csv`. The first three
are declared by `benchmarks/regenerate_track_v3.py`, which this page runs
before drawing anything; the fourth is a hand-staged follow-up with no
declared job of its own. [Provenance](#sec-provenance) says which is which and
why. Nothing is typed into the prose, which is what stops the text and the
tables drifting apart.
:::

## What v2 shipped, and the question nobody asked {#sec-shipped}

[Version 2](../track-construction-v2/index.qmd) replaced the rule behind every
`track_id` published up to OPDI v0.0.2 — group on `(icao24, callsign)`, cut on
a time gap — with one that groups on `icao24` alone and cuts when the
airframe's *last non-blank* callsign genuinely differs from the current one.
The configuration key is `segmentation.method`, and it ships as
`` `r SHIP$method` `` — the production alias for the arm the segmentation
study itself calls `` `r SHIP$resolved` ``, arm A8.

The break exists to separate two real flights of the same airframe once their
callsigns diverge. It was built and measured against that question, and v2's
own evidence — the gain from dropping callsign out of the group key, the small
amount of new merging the break claws back — is about whether *the airframe
splits when it should*. Nobody asked the complementary question: what happens
when the callsign the break fires on turns out not to be a real change at all,
but the aircraft's transponder briefly decoding it wrong and then decoding it
right again? A8 has no way to tell the two apart. It breaks on the first
sample that differs from the last real one it saw, and a flicker satisfies
that test on the way out and again on the way back in — twice for one
airframe that never changed flight.

## The defect, found by elimination {#sec-defect}

The evidence is two independent measurements of the same day,
2026-06-01, agreeing with each other.

**By elimination first.** `recommended`'s break fires on exactly three
conditions: a gap over 30 minutes, a gap over 15 minutes below 5,000 ft, or a
genuine callsign change. The two gap rules cannot produce a track boundary
with a sub-minute gap — their thresholds are fifteen and thirty minutes — so
every sub-minute-gap boundary that day is, by elimination, a callsign break.
Classifying every boundary `recommended` actually draws that day by cause:

```{r boundary-table}
#| echo: false
classes <- c("boundary_gap_gt_30min", "boundary_gap_gt_15min_low_alt",
             "boundary_flicker_revert_leg", "boundary_flicker_excursion_leg",
             "boundary_genuine_callsign_change")
labels  <- c("gap > 30 min", "gap > 15 min & < 5,000 ft",
             "flicker revert leg (Y -> X)", "flicker excursion leg (X -> Y)",
             "genuine callsign change")
bt <- data.frame(
  Cause = labels,
  Boundaries = sapply(classes, function(c) num(FLK(c))),
  Share = sapply(classes, function(c) pct(FLK(paste0(c, "_pct")))),
  check.names = FALSE
)
kable(bt, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
      col.names = c("Cause", "boundaries", "share of all boundaries"),
      caption = paste0("Every track boundary `recommended` draws on ",
                        "2026-06-01, by cause. ", num(FLK("n_boundaries")),
                        " boundaries total."))
```

Of `r num(FLK("callsign_change_boundaries"))` boundaries attributed to a
callsign change, `r num(FLK("boundary_flicker_revert_leg") + FLK("boundary_flicker_excursion_leg"))`
(`r pct(FLK("flicker_attributed_pct"))` of *every* boundary the rule draws, not
just of the callsign-change ones) trace to a flicker's revert or excursion
leg. Only `r num(FLK("boundary_genuine_callsign_change"))` are a genuine
change with nothing reverting either side of it. A flicker does not split a
track once — it **trisects** a flight, tripping the break on the way out
(excursion leg) and again on the way back (revert leg).

`r num(FLK("n_collision"))` boundaries
(`r pct(FLK("collision_pct"))`) match both a flicker's revert leg and the next
flicker's excursion leg at once — an airframe garbling its callsign
repeatedly with no stable sample in between. The two flicker buckets summing
to the same count either way, that collision count is not, on its own, proof
the two are counted disjointly; it is counted rather than assumed.

**The raw sequence confirms it directly.** The elimination argument infers a
flicker from a boundary's shape — sub-minute gap, no altitude signature. The
raw callsign sequence, ignoring blanks, says so outright: a value that differs
from both its predecessor and its successor, whose predecessor and successor
agree with each other (X → Y → X), holds for a median
`r num(FLK("held_p50_s"))` s — the 90th and 99th percentiles are the same
`r num(FLK("held_p90_s"))` s, meaning essentially every flicker is a single
sample — and the longest held only `r num(FLK("held_max_s"))` s. Nothing that
holds for one sample and reverts is a flight changing its callsign; it is a
transponder decoding one message wrong.

## The debounce, and what it costs {#sec-debounce}

`debounced` (arm A9) adds one condition to A8's break: the new callsign must
still be in force `callsign_min_persistence_seconds` later. A flicker fails
that test — the value has already reverted — and a genuine change passes it,
because the new callsign is still there. At `hold = 0` it reproduces
`recommended` exactly, which is what the first row of every table on this
page is.

```{r fragmentation-table}
#| echo: false
ft <- fragm
ft$Arm <- ifelse(ft$arm == "recommended", "recommended (A8, ships)",
                  paste0("debounced (A9), hold=", ft$hold_s, "s"))
ft <- ft[, c("Arm", "tracks", "tracks_per_flight",
             "tracks_2plus_raw_callsigns", "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns")]
ft$tracks <- num(ft$tracks)
ft$tracks_per_flight <- p3(ft$tracks_per_flight)
ft$tracks_2plus_raw_callsigns <- num(ft$tracks_2plus_raw_callsigns)
ft$tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns <- num(ft$tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns)
kable(ft, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr",
      col.names = c("Arm", "tracks", "tracks / flight",
                    "2+ raw callsigns", "2+ PERSISTED callsigns"),
      caption = "2026-06-01, re-segmenting `osn_tracks_clean`. `2+ raw` and `2+ persisted` are per-track callsign counts, not tracks-per-flight.")
```

**Fragmentation falls.** At a 30 s hold the partition drops from
`r num(FRG("recommended", 0, "tracks"))` to `r num(FRG("debounced", 30, "tracks"))`
tracks, `r pct(DROP(30))` fewer — close to twice the roughly 5,100 flickers
[the defect section](#sec-defect) counted, which is the shape a fix should
have: each suppressed flicker removes two boundaries, not one.

**`2+ raw callsigns` rises, and that is expected, not a merge.** A track that
now swallows a flicker legitimately contains both the real callsign and the
transient garble, so distinct-raw-callsign count rises with the hold by
construction. It cannot, on its own, tell a suppressed flicker from a track
that genuinely fused two flights — both look like "more than one callsign in
this track."

**`2+ PERSISTED callsigns` is the guard, and it does not rise.** Counting only
callsigns that individually span at least the hold inside a track — a garble
spans a sample or two, a genuinely fused second flight spans minutes —
`debounced` stays at `r num(FRG("debounced", 15, "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns"))`
to `r num(FRG("debounced", 60, "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns"))` across the
three holds tested, against `recommended`'s
`r num(FRG("recommended", 0, "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns"))` — the same
order of magnitude — and it **shrinks as the hold grows**, from
`r num(FRG("debounced", 15, "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns"))` at 15 s to
`r num(FRG("debounced", 60, "tracks_2plus_persisted_callsigns"))` at 60 s. A
rule that was wrongly fusing distinct flights would show the opposite shape —
more persisted-callsign tracks as it gets more permissive. This one shows
fewer, which is the signature of a debounce swallowing flicker and nothing
else.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What this table cannot measure

`track_fragmentation.py` re-segments `osn_tracks_clean` — state vectors
already cleaned under the boundaries `recommended` produced. A candidate arm
that would have kept a track together never gets the chance to have it
cleaned as one track, so this is a measurement of re-segmenting
already-split data, not of segmenting from raw. For counting tracks that is
second order; it is not the from-raw measurement. [Against
APDF](#sec-apdf) reports the one job that is.
:::

## Genuine-merge neutrality {#sec-genuine}

The guard in [the previous section](#sec-debounce) asks whether the debounce
*creates* new fused flights. A second, sharper question is whether it changes
the count of fusions that were *already there* under `recommended` — the
population `2+ persisted callsigns` cannot separate from noise on its own,
because a dense pair of distinct callsigns each spanning minutes looks
identical whichever arm drew the track.

```{r genuine-table}
#| echo: false
gt <- genuine
gt$Arm <- ifelse(gt$arm == "recommended", "recommended (hold=0)",
                  paste0("debounced (hold=", gt$hold_s, "s)"))
gt <- gt[, c("Arm", "refined_genuine_merges", "ratio_vs_recommended")]
gt$refined_genuine_merges <- num(gt$refined_genuine_merges)
gt$ratio_vs_recommended <- ratio(gt$ratio_vs_recommended)
kable(gt, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrr",
      col.names = c("Arm", "refined genuine two-flight fusions / day",
                    "ratio vs. recommended"),
      caption = "2026-06-01. A genuine fusion: two callsigns in one track, each spanning >= 300s and >= 100 samples, and string-dissimilar (Levenshtein > 2, not a prefix of each other) -- the same floor applied to both arms.")
```

`debounced` fuses `r num(GEN("debounced", "refined_genuine_merges"))` distinct
pairs a day against `recommended`'s
`r num(GEN("recommended", "refined_genuine_merges"))` —
`r ratio(GEN("debounced", "refined_genuine_merges") / GEN("recommended", "refined_genuine_merges"))`
— and the same RYR/EJU consecutive-rotation pairs appear under **both** arms.
The debounce only changes behaviour for callsign excursions that do not
persist; two callsigns that are each genuinely present for minutes look
identical to A8 and A9 alike, so a rule that fuses those pairs is a property
of the shared gap and lookback rules underneath both arms, not something this
fix introduces. The residual is pre-existing, and it is not what this page
was written to fix.

## Against APDF, and the limits of that {#sec-apdf}

**What the reference can and cannot settle.** The obvious check is whether a
merged track's block times agree better with APDF's. It is not available.
`AOBT` and `AIBT` are frequently rounded to the whole minute, so a difference
of tens of seconds measures the reference's quantisation rather than the
detector; and ADS-B presence does not share an end with the block times,
because a transponder may stay on well past on-block or come on well before
off-block. Neither limitation is a defect in APDF — they are what the data
is — but together they mean a timing comparison here would produce a number
with no interpretation.

What survives both limitations is counting and naming. Movement counts per
aerodrome are insensitive to rounding and to transponder dwell. `AP_C_RWY` is
categorical and 100% populated at every aerodrome in the study set. Those are
what this paper asks of APDF, and they are asked as a **guard** rather than as
the result: merging two halves of a cruise-phase split should barely move
either, and a large movement shift would mean the change did something other
than intended.

The improvement itself is measured internally — [fragmentation and milestone
pairing](#sec-debounce) — because those are the quantities the defect
actually damages.

```{r movements-table}
#| echo: false
mt <- moves
mt$Label <- ifelse(mt$label == "recommended",
                    "recommended (opdi-prod, shipped)",
                    "debounced (opdi/research/a9)")
mt <- mt[, c("Label", "opdi_kept_dep_ratio", "opdi_kept_arr_ratio", "guard_verdict")]
mt$opdi_kept_dep_ratio <- ratio(mt$opdi_kept_dep_ratio)
mt$opdi_kept_arr_ratio <- ratio(mt$opdi_kept_arr_ratio)
kable(mt, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrl",
      col.names = c("Warehouse", "departures, OPDI/APDF", "arrivals, OPDI/APDF",
                    "guard"),
      caption = "2026-06-03. Ratios use OPDI's fragments-removed movement count (`MOVEMENT_DEP`/`MOVEMENT_ARR`) against APDF's, the same definition track-construction-v2's payoff regression check uses.")
```

The debounced run lands at
`r ratio(MOV("debounced", "opdi_kept_dep_ratio"))` departures and
`r ratio(MOV("debounced", "opdi_kept_arr_ratio"))` arrivals against APDF, with
`r num(MOV("debounced", "rule_dep_excluded"))` real departures and
`r num(MOV("debounced", "rule_arr_excluded"))` real arrivals wrongly excluded
by the movement rule, and a tighter per-aerodrome spread than the baseline
row. **Guard passed: debouncing does not break movement counting.**

**The honest caveat.** This is not a clean arm delta.
`r MOV("recommended", "caveat")` The guard this section exists to answer —
does debouncing *break* movement counting — is answered no either way; the
recommended row's own departure ratio moving from the historical baseline is
not evidence for or against the debounce, and is not claimed as any.

**What was dropped.** A runway-identity check against `AP_C_RWY` was planned
and not run: APDF's `SAM ID` cannot join the flight-list's track hash, so
there is no key to run the comparison on. It is recorded here as a limitation
rather than left silently absent.

## `track_id` again {#sec-trackid}

::: {.callout-important}
## Not decided here

`debounced` defaults **off**.
`callsign_min_persistence_seconds` ships at `r p2(SHIP$hold_s)`, which
`debounced()`'s own docstring states reproduces `recommended` exactly — the
arm is present in the codebase, validated on this page, and not selected by
any shipped configuration.
:::

[Version 2](../track-construction-v2/index.qmd#sec-continuity) already spent
the cost of one `track_id` discontinuity: A8 hashes a different group key and
suffixes a sample offset instead of a month, so no identifier from before that
release joins to any identifier after it. Promoting A9 to the default would
spend that cost a second time — not because the group key changes again
(`debounced` groups on `icao24`, exactly as `recommended` does), but because
`id_from_start_time` means a track's identifier is derived from its own first
sample, and suppressing a flicker changes which sample that is for every track
a flicker used to cut in two. The count of published identifiers surviving a
promotion would not be zero the way v2's was, but it would not be the
identity map either, and nothing on this page measured how far from it.

That is a decision for the contract owner, weighing a real fragmentation
defect against a second continuity break on a published contract, not a
result this validation page can produce by itself. It is not taken here.

## Limitations

**One day, mostly.** The boundary-cause breakdown, the flicker
holding-time distribution and the fragmentation table are all 2026-06-01. The
APDF movement guard is 2026-06-03. Nothing on this page claims the day is
representative; it is the day Tasks 1, 4 and 5 measured and the day this page
reports.

**Re-segmentation, not re-ingestion, for fragmentation.** [The debounce
section](#sec-debounce) states this in place: `track_fragmentation.py`
re-segments already-cleaned state vectors, whose cleaning was itself
partitioned by `recommended`'s own boundaries. The APDF guard is the one job
here that runs a full pipeline — `run_debounced_day.py`, steps 02 through
04b — from raw.

**The genuine-merge comparison is a hand-run follow-up, not a declared job.**
[Genuine-merge neutrality](#sec-genuine) reads `debounced_vs_recommended_merge.py`'s
output, which Task 4 ran once to interpret the persisted-callsign guard's
residual. It is not wired into `regenerate_track_v3.py` — see
[Provenance](#sec-provenance) for why and what re-declaring it would take.

**Runway identity was dropped, not measured and found equal.** [Against
APDF](#sec-apdf) states why: there is no join key between APDF's `SAM ID` and
the flight list's track hash.

**No downstream milestone comparison.** `debounced` was not scored on
step 04 events or measurements, only on the partition itself and on the
flight list's movement counts. Anything that consumes a track more granularly
than "how many movements landed at this aerodrome" is untested here.

## Provenance note {#sec-provenance}

`flicker_2026.csv`, `fragmentation_2026.csv` and `movements_2026.csv` are
each declared as one job in `benchmarks/regenerate_track_v3.py`
(`flicker_2026`, `fragmentation_2026`, `movements_2026`). All three are staged
here as **hand-transcribed committed values**, not as output of a run this
checkout performed: Tasks 1, 4 and 5 ran `callsign_flicker.py`,
`track_fragmentation.py` and `movement_counts.py` on the cluster at commit
`da2dcde` (`bench: debounce validation scripts (fragmentation residual + APDF
movement guard)`), and the numbers were recorded from those runs rather than
regenerated by this page. `--out-name` support was added to all three scripts
afterward, in the same change that added `regenerate_track_v3.py` itself —
so the code fingerprint the entrypoint checks against has moved on from the
commit that actually produced these figures, and `--check` correctly reports
all three as stale. Re-running them is what clears that, and would write
files this page expects to be identical to the ones committed here, because
nothing in the classification logic changed — only the ability to write a
CSV. This page renders with `OPDI_RENDER=skip` and reports these three
outputs as staged rather than paying a cluster session for a number that
would not move.

`genuine_merge_2026.csv` has no declared job at all. It is
`debounced_vs_recommended_merge.py`'s output, a follow-up Task 4 ran once, by
hand, to interpret `fragmentation_2026.csv`'s persisted-callsign guard column
once that guard showed a nonzero residual. The module docstring in
`regenerate_track_v3.py` records what re-declaring it as a job would need: the
script is read-only and writes nothing a staleness check can key on today, so
wiring it in means giving it the same `--out-name`/`--results-dir` treatment
the other three received, not just adding a `Job` entry.

Every number in this file traces to the working notes for this fix —
`task-6-numbers.md`, under `.superpowers/sdd/` in the `opdi` repository,
dated 2026-09-15 — which is itself a transcription of Tasks 1, 4 and 5's
cluster output. That file, not this one, is the record of how each number was
actually computed; this page's job is to read it consistently, not to
re-derive it.
